description:
Only if the design review accepts the single-owner buffer shape for a prototype. On a prototype/ branch, never merged (as the repo's other prototypes): a `Defk.Buffer.new(i64, n)` returning a reference-backed resource; kernels with a `buf :: buffer(i64)` parameter type that mutate it and return the same reference; Elixir mode keeping the buffer in an ETS table owned by the process; the Bloom filter example (insert batch, query batch) measured against the value-semantics version from the copy-cost ticket and against a pure Elixir Bloom (bit set in a map or :atomics). Tests: agreement property between modes, process death frees the buffer (frames_live-style counter), hot upgrade with a live buffer, forced yields inside a kernel holding a buffer, cross-process call raises.

Report: speed, the test results, and every place the Elixir meaning leaked (an observable difference between modes). The ADR is then accepted or rejected on that evidence.

needs-triage until the review lands.
title: Throwaway prototype: Defk.Buffer on the Bloom filter, with ETS-backed Elixir mode
